title.narrative: Enhancing Collection of Revenue and Expenditure Management Project

description.narrative: The ENCORE remains a well-performing project supporting difficult governance reforms that are critical to the national development priorities of DRC. The proposed Additional Financing will scale up activities to buttress expenditure management reforms implemented under ENCORE and include deepened support for independent oversight arrangements at central level. The AF will also expand support for improved resource management to three additional provinces (Kongo Central, Equateur, and Maniema).
The project development objective is to increase mining revenue transparency and improve expenditure management at the central level and in the project provinces

condition.narrative: SCHEDULE 2, Section I. A.1.b. of the Financing Agreement. The Recipient shall no later than ninety (90) days after the SignatureDate, or such other date as agreed by the Association, select and hire an environmental and social specialist(s) and a gender-basedviolence specialist, all under terms of references, acceptable to the Association

SCHEDULE 2, Section I. A.1.b. of the Financing Agreement. The Recipient shall no later than one hundred twenty (120) days after theEffective Date, or such other date as agreed by the Association, establish within the COREF, and thereafter maintain throughoutProject implementation, sub-office(s) at the provincial level, composed by a technical team led by a PFM specialist in adequatenumbers and with terms of reference, acceptable to the Association

SCHEDULE 2, Section I. A.1.c. of the Financing Agreement. The Recipient shall no later than one hundred twenty (120) days after theEffective Date, or such other date as agreed by the Association, establish, and thereafter maintain throughout Projectimplementation, a national PFM reform steering committee (“National PFM Reform Steering Committee”) with terms of referenceacceptable to the Association

SCHEDULE 2, Section I. A.1.d. of the Financing Agreement. The Recipient shall no later than one hundred twenty (120) days after theEffective Date, or such other date as agreed by the Association, establish, and thereafter maintain throughout Projectimplementation, technical working groups (“Technical Working Groups”), each with terms of reference acceptable to the Association

SCHEDULE 2, Section I. A.1.e. of the Financing Agreement. The Recipient shall no later than one hundred twenty (120) days after theEffective Date, or such other date as agreed by the Association, ensure the establishment, and thereafter maintenance throughoutProject implementation, of a provincial PFM reform steering committee in each of the Project Provinces (“Provincial PFM ReformSteering Committee”) with terms of reference, composition and powers acceptable to the Association

SCHEDULE 2, Section I. C.1.b. of the Financing Agreement. The Recipient shall no later than one hundred eighty (180) days after theEffective Date, or such other date as agreed by the Association, but in any event prior to making any Performance Bonuses, selectand hire an independent auditor (“Auditor”) under terms of reference acceptable to the Association

SCHEDULE 2, Section I. D.a. of the Financing Agreement. The Recipient shall no later than 120 days after the Effective Date, orsuch other date as agreed by the Association, appoint the IGF as the Recipient's agency, or any other entity as agreed between theRecipient and the Association, responsible for verifying the data and other evidence supporting the achievement of one or more PBCsas set forth in the PBC Manual and recommending corresponding payments to be made, as applicable.

target.value: FFG's Revised Decree is satisfactorily implemented and Inter-ministerial Decree for 0.3% sharing is satisfactorily implemented

actual.value: The Decree for 0.3% sharing was approved in december 2021 and decree modifying FOMIN was approved in February 2023, and they are being satisfactorily implemented.

title.narrative: Annual Budget Review Reports approved and published for Central Government and for selected provinces

target.value: Central Government 2025 annual budget review report published by end of September 2026

actual.value: The CoA published on its website the 2022 budget execution reports of the four project provinces in November 2023, and 2022 budget execution report of the Central Government in April 2024. The 2023 budget execution reports of the four project provinces have been produced by provincial governments but have not yet been submitted to the CoA. Publication of the Central Governmentâ€™s 2023 budget execution report is expected by the end of September 2024.

target.value: The TSA Action Plan is implemented satisfactorily to the Bank

actual.value: The TSA Action Plan has undergone significant delays.

target.value: IFMIS platform is deployed at least in two additional central line ministries

title.narrative: Up-to-date database on household living conditions at national level available

title.narrative: Satisfactory digital solutions for revenue collection and management established in project provinces

target.value: Satisfactorily digital solutions are available in all four project provinces

actual.value: No digital solutions for revenue collection and management have yet been developed.

title.narrative: Consolidated, relevant, and comprehensive budget reports and financial statements in project provinces are produced and available

target.value: Quarterly budget reports are prepared and regularly published on all four project provinces websites and financial reports meeting new accounting standards are produced by existing DGTCP provincial units, then submitted to CoA
